candidates.title: Recurrent Attention-based Token Selection for Efficient Streaming Video-LLMs
candidates.abstract: Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) excel at understanding videos in-context, provided they have full access to the video when answering queries. However, these models face challenges in streaming scenarios where hour-long videos must be processed online, and questions need timely responses. In this work, we propose a training-free approach compatible with standard Video-LLMs, leveraging three key concepts: 1) LLM-informed selection of visual tokens to identify those that the LLM has attended to and contributed to its understanding of each short clip. Our attention-based selection allows us to discard up to ~95% of unimportant visual tokens with minimal performance loss; 2) Recurrent processing of past selected tokens to generate temporally coherent understanding of each processed clip; 3) Caption-based question answering for lightweight and accurate responses. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on streaming video benchmarks, striking a balance between efficiency and effectiveness.
candidates.reason: ストリーミングVideo-LLM向けに、LLMが注意した視覚トークンを再帰的に選択保持し重要でない視覚トークンを最大約95％破棄する学習不要の手法で、時間的一貫性を保ちながらストリーミング動画推論の計算量を削減しており、トークン選択による推論効率化に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: SAID: Accelerating Diffusion-Based Language Models via Scaffold-Aware Iterative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Diffusion large language models (DLLMs) enable non-autoregressive generation by iteratively denoising corrupted token sequences with bidirectional context. Despite their ability to update multiple positions in parallel, inference remains costly due to the many denoising steps required for high-quality generation. We propose SAID, a Scaffold-Aware Iterative Decoding framework that accelerates DLLMs by reallocating computation across tokens. SAID first spends denoising computation on scaffold tokens to establish the coarse semantic structure, and then completes predictable detail tokens with fewer steps. We further adapt SAID to block-wise diffusion decoding and introduce Confidence-Hierarchical Layered Generation (CHLG), which assigns additional steps only to low-confidence tokens. Experiments on LLaDA-8B and LLaDA 1.5 across math, coding, and knowledge benchmarks show that SAID significantly accelerates DLLM inference with a maximum speedup of 9.1x while maintaining competitive performance. Our code is publicly available: https://github.com/TH-AI-Lab-PKU/SAID.
candidates.reason: SAIDは拡散型LLM向けに、まず足場トークンへ去ノイズ計算を配分し予測可能な詳細トークンを少ないステップで補完する scaffold-aware 反復デコードと、低信頼トークンへだけ追加ステップを与える階層生成で最大9.1倍の高速化を示しており、拡散LLMのデコード高速化に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
candidates.reason: FoveaTreeは領域マージによる特徴歪みから密度マップを作る四分木誘導と、木構造を継承する注意剪定の二段で視覚トークンを保持率10％まで削減する学習不要の剪定枠組みで、Video LLM推論の視覚トークン計算削減に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: LLM-Rank: A Graph Theoretical Approach to Pruning Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: The evolving capabilities of large language models are accompanied by growing sizes and deployment costs, necessitating effective inference optimisation techniques. We propose a novel pruning method utilising centrality measures from graph theory, reducing both the computational requirements and the memory footprint of these models. Specifically, we devise a method for creating a weighted directed acyclical graph representation of multilayer perceptrons to which we apply a modified version of the weighted PageRank centrality measure to compute node importance scores. In combination with uniform pruning this leads to structured sparsity. We call this pruning method MLPRank. Furthermore we introduce an extension to decoder-only transformer models and call it LLMRank. For both variants we demonstrate a strong performance. With MLPRank on average leading to 6.09 % higher accuracy retention than three popular baselines and 13.42 % with LLMRank compared to two popular baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/amazon-science/llm-rank-pruning.
candidates.reason: LLM-Rank（MLPRank）はMLPを重み付き有向非循環グラフとして表し修正PageRank中心性でノード重要度を測る構造化剪定で、計算要求とメモリフットプリントを同時に削減し精度保持で既存剪定を上回るため、推論最適化のためのモデル圧縮に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Cascade: Token-Sharded Private LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: As LLMs continue to increase in parameter size, the computational resources required to run them are available to fewer parties. Therefore, third-party inference services -- where LLMs are hosted by third parties with significant computational resources -- are becoming increasingly popular. However, third party inference raises critical concerns about user data privacy. To mitigate these risks, privacy researchers have developed provably secure schemes for third-party inference, such as Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC). However, SMPC protocols have significant computational and communication overhead, and do not scale to large models. In this work, we propose a new multi-party inference protocol, Cascade, that avoids these punitive costs by leveraging sharding in the sequence dimension to maintain privacy, trading off cryptographic privacy guarantees for increased performance and scalability. We demonstrate that Cascade is resistant to a generalization of a recent attack that is highly effective against other statistical privacy schemes, and that it is further resistant to learning-based attacks. As Cascade is orders of magnitude faster than existing schemes, our findings offer practical solutions for secure deployment of modern state-of-the-art LLMs.
candidates.reason: Cascadeは第三者推論サービスのプライバシー保護のため、系列次元でトークンをシャーディングするマルチパーティ推論プロトコルで、SMPCの莫大な計算・通信オーバーヘッドを避け桁違いに高速であると示されており、プライベートLLM推論の実行方式に直接貢献する。
